to raise your hand. To withdraw your question, press star one again. I will now hand the conference over to Omar Saad, Head of Investor Relations and Capital Markets. Please go ahead.

Omar Saad

Head of Investor Relations and Capital Markets, Amer Sports
Welcome, everyone. Thanks for joining Amer Sports earnings call for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026. Earlier this morning, we announced our financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and the release can be found on our IR website, investors.amersports.com. A quick reminder to everyone that today's call will contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws. These forward-looking statements reflect our current expectations and beliefs only.
They are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please see the safe harbor statement in our earnings release and SEC filings. We will also discuss certain non-IFRS financial measures. Please refer to our earnings release for important information regarding such non-IFRS financial measures, including reconciliations to the most comparable IFRS financial measures.
We will begin with prepared remarks from our CEO, James Zheng, and CFO, Andrew Page, followed by a Q&A session until 9:00 A.M. Eastern. Arc'teryx CEO Stuart Haselden and Salomon CEO Guillaume Meyzenq will join for the Q&A session. With that, I will turn the call over to James.

James Zheng

CEO, Amer Sports
Thanks, Omar. Our global momentum continued in Q3 with 24% revenue growth and a strong operating margin expansion. All segments, geographies, and the channel achieved double-digit growth, led by another exceptional quarter from Salomon Softgoods, a very solid Arc'teryx omni-comp, and a continued strong growth for Wilson Tennis 360. Given our excellent results year-to-date and a strong start to the fourth quarter, we expect 2026 to be another excellent year for Amer Sports.
Looking forward beyond this year, given the broad-based momentum across our portfolio, the healthy premium sports and outdoor markets, and our world-class team, I am very confident in the future look for our company. I will start with key highlights from our three segments. First, technical apparel. Arc'teryx delivered another great quarter with broad-based strengths across regions, channels, and the categories. Strong technical apparel direct-to-consumer momentum was driven by a 16% omni-comp.
In Q3, Arc'teryx had a huge brand moment with the launch of Sperro SV, our latest and the most pinnacle hardshell jacket. The Sperro SV represents a major leap forward in technical innovation and circular design. Made with recycled and recyclable materials, it is also our most advanced hardshell jacket, pushing the limits of pinnacle technical performance.
Sperro is also our first product under System 0, which is a groundbreaking new framework and the business model for designing, manufacturing, repairing, and regenerating technical apparel. The launch generated record visibility and engagement across social media, traditional media, community activations, billboards, and the content creators. The consumer response has been very strong too, with one in four Sperro buyers coming totally new to the brand.
The launch is also having a strong halo effect on our overall hardshell category.
Another big brand moment was the new collection to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Arc'teryx's collaboration with BEAMS, the iconic Japanese retailers and the cultural institution. The capsule was widely successful, almost selling out in the first 72 hours, with especially strong buzz in North America and APAC. From a category standpoint, I first want to highlight women's, which continues to grow faster than any other category for Arc'teryx.
We are seeing momentum with female consumers across all channels, regions, and products. Women's only models and seasonal colorways continue to be a key growth driver, accounting for 50% of women's sales in Q3. Our Clarkia franchise, which combines technical performance fabric with modern updated silhouettes, continues to stand out with our female consumers.
We began with our Clarkia pant model two years ago, and now we have five different products in the franchise, including the recently released Clarkia AR pant and the Clarkia AR Insulated Hoody. Turning to footwear, which had another great quarter with strong overall momentum driven by existing lines, as well as the launch of the Kopec 2, our most popular hiking shoes. Arc'teryx had a big footwear brand moment at UTMB with an exclusive colorway of the Sylan 2 trail running shoes.
This drove energy to the franchise and highlighting the race shoes in the pinnacle week of the trail running season. Arc'teryx athlete, Jazmine Lowther, was a top five finisher wearing Sylan 2.
More recently, at the beginning of Q4, we launched the Postour Boot, which is an insulated waterproof recovery boot that has a removable built-in slipper designed to wear after a hard day of skiing. This unique product has gained strong traction in social media, and the men's product is sold out across most sizes. Turning to our Veilance sub-brand, which continued to have solid growth in Q3 from a small base.
We continue to focus on investing in units, developing our collections, expanding distribution, and improving the e-coms experience. On the mountain, Arc'teryx hosted two academies in Q3, including Chamonix, France, and Squamish, Canada. Both were great successes, with over 45,000 visitors in total in the village over the weekend and more than 1,300 attendees in clinics. Turning to Peak Performance, which delivered solid growth in Q3.
The reposition to a full-price premium outdoor brand continues to progress, with more focused product categories and assortments. We are seeing some early green shoots in China as we improve fit and the focused assortment. There will also be a Peak Performance pop-up in NoLIta in New York City this December. Turning to the Outdoor Performance segment, which was led by another outstanding quarter from Salomon Softgoods.
The investments we are making to grow Salomon brand awareness and the distribution footprint are paying off, driving strong footwear momentum across regions and channels for both Sportstyle and the performance products. Starting with Sportstyle, which continues to see great momentum. The XT-6 and XT-Whisper franchises are resonating with a younger and more diverse audience. In Q3, we launched a new, more premium evolution of Sportstyle with the XT-Evo.
The XT-Evo has seen great traction so far in key epicenters, especially with a younger audience. This latest iteration is part of our robust pipeline of Sportstyle franchises development plan. We also recently launched our global Salomon winter campaign, starring our global brand ambassador, superstar singer and actress, Jisoo. She is helping us drive brand heat across all major regions, especially in epicenter cities.
For example, in China, we launched a market-specific campaign with Jisoo called "Blue Perspective." Jisoo drew a huge crowd when she attended our recent flagship opening in Beijing, which resonated extremely well with younger female consumers and generated two billion impressions in one month. Moving to our performance lines, which are also working very well. Performance consumers increasingly recognize Salomon as an all-terrain brand, from trail to gravel to roads and cities.
We continue to develop cutting-edge performance products, including the recently launched second generation of S/Lab Genesis, a highly technical trail shoe. We launched this shoe during the UTMB Mont-Blanc with a full week of activations in the village. At UTMB, Salomon represented one in five shoes worn and two of every three hydration packs. As we further develop Salomon in the running category, we are thrilled to become the IRONMAN global premium partner beginning 2027.
We believe Salomon is uniquely positioned to bring its heritage in mountain, trail, and road to the world's most iconic endurance community. IRONMAN is a natural extension for Salomon, given its endurance legacy in cross-country skiing, adventure racing, and trail running. Looking at Salomon regionally, the brand continues to have excellent brand heat everywhere. In Greater China, we continue to deliver very strong double-digit growth, driven by strength across Sportstyle, performance, and apparel.
Our local-for-local apparel and accessories line in China continues to gain strong traction. For the second year in a row, we hosted the Shanghai Gravel Running Event, which has grown rapidly in popularity and had 4x the sign-up versus last year. Salomon is also experiencing surging demand in Korea, Japan, and Australia, supported by global marketing campaigns and unique local activation that deepen consumer engagement and cultural relevancy. Moving to Europe, where we are experiencing strong demand.
Sportstyle continues to be the biggest growth driver, but gravel is also gaining momentum in Europe, supported by marketing campaigns, in-store, and running event activations. We are seeing high e-comm growth in Europe, even as we expand our premium direct-to-consumer and wholesale footprint. We are also seeing strong performance in our local epicenters, especially Paris and London.
Lastly, I will mention the U.S., which is the largest single sneaker market in the world, but still a small business for us. We know there is a strong demand for Salomon here, but still very limited distribution for consumers to find our products. Today, we are seeing a clear acceleration in North America as we leverage the rising brand awareness to expand distribution with both new and existing wholesale partners, as well as our own stores and e-commerce. Some of our local U.S.
activations in Q3 include Gravel Lounge L.A., the XT-Evo launch at Kith, and an XT-6 and XT-Whisper collaboration with Free People. Across all markets, our epicenter strategy is working. Our tier 1 global epicenters, Paris, London, Shanghai, Beijing, Tokyo, New York, and Los Angeles, are all driving very strong sales momentum and rising brand awareness.
In the U.S., New York and Los Angeles have some of the youngest Salomon buyers across all markets. Looking ahead, we plan to expand the Epicenter approach to Berlin, Seoul, Miami, San Francisco, Chicago, and Boston. Lastly, before I switch to Ball & Racquet, I also want to mention our winter sports equipment franchises, which had a very strong Q3 with strong shipment to start the season and solid order books for the winter season overall.
We are pleased that our brands continue taking share in the highly competitive markets. Our Atomic and Armada President, Wolfgang Mayrhofer, is retiring after 41 years at the company. Current Atomic and Armada CFO, Michael Absmaier, will take over as President beginning in January. I want to thank Wolfgang for four great decades at Atomic, which has more than doubled in size the last 10 years under his leadership.
We are confident that the business won't skip a beat with Michael Absmaier stepping into the President role, given his 22 years at the company and in the industry, including the last three years as CFO of Atomic and Armada. Moving to Ball & Racquet highlights. Ball & Racquet sales growth 12% in Q3, driven by continued strength in Tennis 360, both soft goods and the racquets.
Our Tennis 360 strategy continues to resonate very well with consumers, from unique lines of tennis apparel and footwear to high-performance racquets. Wilson Softgoods continues its exceptional growth trajectory, led by China and APAC, and our performance racquets are continuing to gain market share, led by our two recent launches, the Defyer and the Blade v10. Defyer was ranked the number one performance racquet in the U.S. in September, and the Blade v10 also continues to perform very well.
Wilson now has nine out of 15 top-selling racquets in the U.S. tennis specialty market. With that, I will turn it over to Andrew.

Andrew Page

CFO, Amer Sports
Thank you, James. We had a great financial performance in Q3 across the P&L. The investments we have been making are paying off, driving strong momentum across each of our three biggest opportunities: Arc'teryx, Salomon Softgoods, and Wilson Tennis 360. Amer Sports Group generated Q3 sales growth of 24%, or 23% excluding currency. The strong group sales performance was led by outdoor performance and technical apparel. Ball & Racquet also delivered solid double-digit sales growth.
By channel, the group continues to be driven by D2C, which grew 36%. Wholesale grew 15%, led by Salomon and Arc'teryx. Growth was also very strong across all geographies, led by Asia Pacific, which increased 48%, and China, which grew 30%. The Americas grew 22%, and EMEA grew 10%. Turning to profitability.
Adjusted gross margin increased 150 basis points to 59.4% in Q3, primarily driven by favorable channel, segment, region, and product mix, as well as less discounting and off-price sales. This was slightly offset by higher inbound freight and fuel surcharges tied to the rising cost of oil. Adjusted SG&A expenses as a percentage of revenue increased 80 basis points and represented 43.1% of revenues in Q3, a better rate than implied by our previous guidance.
However, as I will discuss with guidance, some of this upside relates to a shift in timing of SG&A spend from Q3 into Q4. By segment, slight SG&A leverage in outdoor performance was more than offset by slight deleverage at technical apparel, driven by investments in Peak Performance, and deleverage at Ball & Racquet due to investments in Wilson Tennis 360.
Corporate expenses were $61 million, up from $45 million in Q3 last year, mostly related to higher personnel and IT expenses as we modernize our warehouse management and end-to-end planning capabilities and e-comm platforms. This equates to a 70 basis point increase in our adjusted operating margin from 15.7% last year to 16.4% in Q3 of the current year.
Adjusted net finance cost in the quarter was $14 million, and our Q3 adjusted income tax expense was $88 million, which equates to an adjusted effective tax rate of 26%. Adjusted net income in Q3 was $250 million, compared to $185 million in the prior year period. Adjusted diluted earnings per share was $0.42, compared to $0.33 last year. Now turning to segment results. Technical apparel revenues increased 26% to $861 million, led by Arc'teryx.
Growth was fueled by 32% D2C expansion, including a 16% omni-comp. Technical apparel wholesale revenues grew 14%. In Q3, we opened net nine new Arc'teryx stores globally, bringing us to 17 year-to-date. We continue to plan to open 30- 35 net new Arc'teryx stores for the full year of 2026 across all markets. Regionally, the technical apparel growth rate was led by APAC and North America, followed by Greater China and EMEA. In APAC, we saw very strong growth driven by great success in Korea and Japan.
The strong growth in Q3 in Korea was driven by strong retail demand, tourism, and improved product availability. We are very excited for the potential of Arc'teryx in Korea, which we consider to be one of the best outdoor markets in the world, with very high outdoor spending per capita, but still a small market for us.
We also plan to open a major new flagship in Seoul in the fall of 2027. This four-level Alpha location will be the first in the world to rival our Shanghai Museum flagship in terms of size, scale, and overall presence. In North America, Arc'teryx has had a fantastic year so far, and growth continued to be very strong in Q3, including strong double-digit omni-comps in the region.
We are seeing strong traction in both brand stores and e-commerce traffic as we leverage brand experience and community to unlock higher conversion in the U.S. Q3 store openings include the relocation of our first-ever store in Sainte-Catherine, Montreal, to a beautiful 10,000 sq ft space over three floors that offers Veilance and ReBIRD. Another important retail highlight is our Whistler Mountain Town store in Canada, after relocating to a larger space in a better location.
We believe the improved Whistler store can rival our Banff Mountain Town shop, which is one of the highest volume stores in all of North America. Most recently, in early Q4, we opened two important stores in California, a new flagship in the Valley Fair Mall in San Jose, and a new store concept on Abbot Kinney Boulevard in L.A., our first climbing-focused store.
It features an indoor climbing wall and an open-air patio, creating not just a key retail space for this community, but a place for them to climb, gather, and return to. We now have 77 total stores in North America, a count we believe could reach 200-plus stores over time. Greater China continued to deliver strong growth and maintain exceptional profitability in Q3.
We are executing premium channel expansion with new and upgraded stores in high-tier cities and travel hubs while maintaining best-in-class productivity.
We finished Q3 with 144 Arc'teryx stores in Greater China, including owned and franchise partner doors, and we believe this could be 200 doors over time. We are planning 12 net new store openings in Greater China for the full year of 2026, and have opened six net new stores year-to-date. EMEA, which remains Arc'teryx's most under-penetrated market, had solid growth in Q3 despite slower tourist traffic. We saw a lot of brand momentum around mountain activations from UTMB and the Arc'teryx Alpine Academy.
We now have 20 stores across EMEA, and we believe the market could support 75-plus over the long term. Technical apparel adjusted operating margin expanded 210 basis points to 21.1%. Margin growth was led by strong gross margin expansion, driven by favorable material costs, lower inbound air freight usage, as well as product mix. SG&A had slight deleverage, driven by investments in Peak Performance.
Moving to outdoor performance, which saw revenues increase 27% to $917 million, driven by continued very strong performance in Salomon footwear and apparel. By channel, outdoor performance D2C grew 48%, led by new doors and higher productivity across markets, especially the Americas, APAC, and Greater China. Outdoor performance achieved a 28% omni-comp, with strength in both stores and e-commerce. E-commerce is continuing to grow across regions, driven by Sportstyle momentum and higher traffic.
Wholesale grew 18%, driven by strong sell-through and reorders for Sportstyle, as well as door count expansion. Regionally, the outdoor performance growth rate was led by APAC, Greater China, and the Americas, followed by EMEA.
As Salomon cements itself as the modern mountain sports culture brand, demand for its unique all-terrain footwear offering is inflecting globally, and we are doing everything we can to ensure we are positioned to fully develop this large opportunity in the right way across markets. In Asia, D2C continues to be the critical growth channel for Salomon, led by our highly productive Salomon shops.
We opened 15 net new Salomon shops in Greater China this quarter, including both owned stores and franchise partner doors, bringing our total count at quarter end to nearly 330 doors. We expect to open around 50 net new stores in Greater China this year, as we focus on both expanding our fleet and upgrading it with larger format, more productive doors in the highest traffic shopping centers.
The larger format also gives us the space to incorporate footwear and our new apparel offerings, which James mentioned is gaining momentum. We see the potential for Salomon to have 400 doors- 500 doors in China long term. In APAC, where Salomon is also experiencing explosive growth, we opened net seven new stores in Q3 across Japan and Australia.
The overall brand awareness and the desirability of Salomon's footwear offering is growing very rapidly across Asia, and we are also seeing very strong performance from the local apparel line in Korea. In EMEA, key epicenters Paris and London are continuing to see strong growth. We are also further expanding into other European key cities, including a Barcelona shop that opened in July and Liverpool that opened in September.
In the Americas, as James mentioned, Salomon Footwear is continuing to see a material growth acceleration.
The brand is seeing great D2C demand in stores and e-comm for both Sportstyle and performance. We are pleased to see traffic up strongly in e-comm, which tracks our expanding geographic presence, distribution, and awareness across key cities. We are also seeing very strong results across our expanded retail footprint in the U.S., driven by Sportstyle.
Our new Flatiron New York store has performed very well since its grand opening in July, and as we expand our Los Angeles epicenter, we are planning a Beverly Hills location later this year. Salomon has also been seeing very strong wholesale demand in North America. As we shared last call, Salomon has began to expand into a small number of key wholesale doors in epicenter cities with important modern premium sneaker retailers such as Nordstrom, Foot Locker, and JD Sports.
Our sell-through performance has been very strong, and we will continue to thoughtfully and selectively expand with these and other modern sneaker retail channels over the next couple of years. Lastly, our winter sports equipment franchises had a very strong Q3 with solid order books for the winter season overall and strong shipments so far. We are pleased with our continued market share gains despite a competitive market.
The demand for ski vacations in the mountains remains high and consistent, and the core alpine on-piste market is healthy despite inconsistent snow conditions. Many top ski resorts now have excellent snow-making capabilities, and others are investing heavily to build up the infrastructure.
Outdoor performance adjusted operating profit margin expanded 80 basis points from last year to 23.1% in Q3, driven by gross margin expansion from mix shift benefits and slight SG&A leverage on strong sales, as well as shifting some expenses from Q3 into Q4. Moving to Ball & Racquet, where revenue increased 12% to $391 million, driven by soft goods and rackets. This is a more normalized growth level compared to the 24% in Q2, which was unusually strong, driven by the new racket launch sell-ins.
By category, we continue to see very strong momentum in Tennis 360 globally. Growth was led by soft goods, and performance rackets continues to be strong following recent launches. We are also seeing demand for padel products gaining momentum. Beyond rackets, we also saw strong growth in inflatable balls.
Baseball growth was flat, while golf was a slight drag as healthy growth in the pro clubs category was more than offset due to challenges in the commercial clubs in Europe, where traffic was impacted by the World Cup and the heat waves. Regionally, Ball & Racquet growth was led by Greater China, followed by APAC and the Americas. EMEA was a slight drag to growth due to slower sales in golf, as I mentioned. We opened 10 net new Wilson brand stores in Q3, with the majority in Greater China.
We have extensive store opening plans for China long term, given the performance of existing Wilson Tennis 360 shops there. For the full year of 2026, we continue to plan to open approximately 40 net new Wilson Tennis 360 shops in China between owned and partner doors.
In APAC, Wilson delivered solid growth led by continued momentum in soft goods, particularly in Japan and Australia. In North America, we saw strong growth in rackets and team sports. We also continued to expand our Tennis 360 offering into more Dick's Sporting Goods locations, including House of Sport, and are now in 450 Dick's stores with full head-to-toe-to-hand offerings. We also recently opened our first brand store in Miami in the Aventura Mall, which is off to a very strong start.
Ball & Racquet segment adjusted operating profit margin decreased 210 basis points to 6.1%. The margin compression was mainly driven by higher SG&A, reflecting our intentional decision to invest behind Wilson soft goods, including tennis tour pros.
Ball & Racquet gross margin declined slightly as mix and pricing benefits were more than offset by the combined impact of lacking one-time benefits from the change in inventory reserve estimate in the prior year and margin headwinds in baseball bats, as our lower-margin product lines are significantly outperforming. Turning to the group balance sheet. We ended the quarter with $594 million of net cash and exited the quarter with inventories up 16% year-over-year, well below our 24% sales growth.
We are very comfortable with the level and quality of our inventory and happy to see the inventory levels normalize versus revenues as planned. Driven by strong profit growth and disciplined working capital management, we generated $514 million of operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2026, compared to $104 million last year.
For the full year of 2026, we continue to expect to generate solid operating cash flow growth versus 2025. Before guidance, I want to discuss our capital allocation update. Even as we aggressively reinvest in our brands to support long-term sustainable growth, we are still building a significant cash balance and expect to generate billions more free cash flow in the coming five years.
In addition to regular buybacks to offset dilution from our annual long-term incentive plans, the open-ended share repurchase authorization announced today also gives us the flexibility to execute opportunistic buybacks if our share price becomes dislocated from business fundamentals or large supply opportunities arise. Now moving to guidance. Let's begin with the updated full year 2026 outlook. Our guidance assumes current tariff rates remain in place for the remainder of 2026.
We have received substantially all of our tariff refund submission amount in the second quarter of 2026, and any remaining receipts will be negligible. We are raising our 2026 revenue growth guidance from approximately 24% to 25%-26%, which includes an approximate 200 basis point currency benefit at current exchange rates. This implies a 17%-20% growth rate for the fourth quarter. By segment, we are raising our technical apparel 2026 revenue growth guidance from approximately 25%-26% to 27%-28%.
We are also increasing our outdoor performance sales growth expectations from 27%-28% to 28%-29%. Our Ball & Racquet sales growth guidance goes from approximately 14% to 14%-15%. Turning to margins. For 2026, we are narrowing our full year adjusted gross margin guidance from 60.5%-61% to approximately 60.8%, which implies 59.3% in Q4.
We are raising our adjusted operating margin guidance from 14.2%-14.5% to 14.5%-14.7%, which implies approximately 11.5%-12.5% operating margin for Q4. Please note that roughly half of the $65 million net tariff refund received this year relates to 2025, or roughly 40 basis points of our 2026 adjusted gross and operating margin. In other words, the underlying adjusted gross margin in our updated full year 2026 guidance, excluding tariff refunds related to 2025, is 60.4%.
Our underlying 2026 operating margin guide, excluding tariff refunds related to 2025, is 14.1%-14.3%. As you run your models, you will see this implies a lower Q4 adjusted operating margin than we previously expected, driven by a higher SG&A rate. About half of the higher SG&A spend in Q4, or approximately $30 million, is incremental investment to drive our three growth engines.
The other half relates to the timing of expenses that had been planned in Q3 but will now hit Q4. We have high confidence to make these type of opportunistic investments in our brands and capabilities, including marketing, talent, IT, store openings, and digital. We are seeing excellent returns on our investments, both financially and in the form of stronger brand equity. Corporate expense is expected to be approximately $260 million for the full year.
By segment, we are raising technical apparel adjusted operating margin guidance from approximately 22.5% to 23%-23.2%. For outdoor performance, we are raising adjusted operating margin guidance from 16%-16.5% to 17%-17.2%. For Ball & Racquet, we are lowering the adjusted operating margin from 6.7%-7.2% to approximately 6%, predominantly due to reinvestments in Wilson Tennis 360, as well as the negative mix shift in baseball bats.
We are assuming 2026 net finance costs of approximately $80 million. We now assume an effective tax rate of 27%, down from 28%, due to jurisdictional mix shift of earnings. Other operating income should be approximately $58 million for the full year. The IT investments include a new warehouse management system, ERP investments, and a new end-to-end planning system for our brands to improve our planning visibility and agility, which will drive more accurate inventory planning.
Net income attributable to non-controlling interest is expected to be approximately $35 million for the full year. We now expect adjusted diluted EPS of $1.32-$1.35, versus our prior guidance of $1.27-$1.30, which is based on approximately 587 million fully diluted shares. Other full year modeling items to consider.
We are assuming depreciation and amortization of approximately $450 million, including approximately $220 million of ROU depreciation. CapEx is still expected to be approximately $400 million, primarily to support our retail expansion and our IT infrastructure investments. As we begin to look beyond this year, we are also confident in our initial 2027 outlook.
At the group level, our initial outlook is for revenue at the midpoint of our long-term algorithm of low double digit to mid-teens annual growth, and we expect to deliver adjusted operating margin expansion at the low end of our long-term group algorithm of 30 basis points- 70 basis points of annual margin expansion. Please note, we are using the midpoint of our latest 2026 guidance as the base for next year, excluding the 40 basis points of tariff refunds related to 2025 that I mentioned earlier.
Keep in mind that since 2022, we have expanded our gross margin by over 1,000 basis points. This has enabled us to reinvest in our brands from a position of strength over the last four years at a challenging time for others in the industry, without sacrificing operating margin expansion, which has increased roughly 150 basis points per year on average, well above our 30 basis points- 70 basis points long-term algorithm.
Today, given the significant value creation potential for each of our three growth engines, as well as our growing confidence in our significant long-term potential, we want to build the right foundation for our company to scale into a much bigger size, and we want the flexibility to invest in our brands to drive sustainable growth and ensure strong brand equity long term.
This means making investments to attract and retain high-quality talent, support our brands with best-in-class marketing, build out our premium own store network, and develop strong IT and digital platforms. Lastly, should better-than-anticipated demand materialize, we believe we are well-positioned to deliver financial performance ahead of our expectations. With that, I'll turn it back over to the operator for questions.

Operator
We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star one again. We ask that you pick up your handset when asking a question, and if you are muted locally, please remember to unmute your device. Your first question comes from the line of Michael Binetti from Evercore ISI. Please go ahead.

Michael Binetti

Analyst, Evercore ISI
Hey, guys. Great quarter. Really happy to see the buyback. I really think that goes a long way to support the algorithm you guys walked us through in Annecy. Very happy to see it. It was also good to see the Americas grow 22%, considering the tough 34% compare a year ago. So that is a lot more contribution coming from Americas today than what we have seen in the last few years. Obviously, there is more going on in this market.
Could maybe just break that market down a little bit and zero in on where the growth is coming from the core brands? And then maybe any comment you could offer on expanding on the strong start to the fourth quarter. What region or segment are you seeing that in the most?
We see a lot of concerning data points on the market in China, so just thoughts there would be helpful. Appreciate it.

Andrew Page

CFO, Amer Sports
Hey, Michael. Hi, this is Andrew Page. Thank you for the Michael, hi, this is Andrew. Thanks for the feedback. As you pointed out, obviously, you see some continued growth in the Americas and North America. And just remember, that is a focus of ours, and especially in our growth engines of Arc'teryx and Salomon. These are markets that we have focused on. They were immature, comparatively speaking, in some other areas. And so we are excited about what we see with Arc'teryx there.
We have amplified our store build-out there, and those things are well. And at the same time, you can see, and I will let Stuart and both Guillaume jump in, you can see obviously our soft goods, led by footwear, is inflecting in North America as well. Stuart?
Stuart Haselden

CEO, Arc'teryx
Yeah. Thanks, Andrew. Michael, we're seeing really strong progress in North America, in the U.S. specifically. I'll remind you, we have roughly the same number of stores in the U.S. as we have in Canada, and the size of our business between Canada and the U.S. is roughly the same, which makes it very apparent the potential that we have to expand in the U.S.
We focused on building brand awareness and momentum in what we call key epicenters in New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Chicago, and this is working. We're seeing improvement in brand awareness, accelerating traffic and comp trends across all those key markets. It's giving us confidence to continue to invest and look at what the next markets can be for us to expand into. But we're seeing strength across all our product categories.
We see the U.S. specifically as likely our largest market opportunity into the next several years with a clear runway of growth.

Guillaume Meyzenq

CEO, Salomon
As far as Salomon is concerned, I think that this is really the result of the outcome of our strategy and action plan, and the investment we have made from the last, I would say, the last three years. We diligently moved to focusing on the epicenter, of course, New York and L.A., and it's very visible because we're opening store. But what you should understand is a full multi-layer investment we are making on community activation in Sportstyle and in running.
It's investment in media, out of home and digital media, and of course, the traction with the store. So footwear is really driving a very strong performance.
What is new or more visible in this quarter is the fact that we also engage with much more doors with athletic specialty or premium sneaker doors from the last quarter, and the sell-through is going very well. We solidified the partnership with our partner. We do it also very diligently so that it's door by door.
